messages.content: We are looking at Pittsburgh for the June 12-15 weekend, the three of us. The baseball game is Saturday at 1:35, and we want the Carnegie Science Center on Sunday. Compare driving from Chicago with flying, but do not buy anything.
I can compare the full door-to-door time and cost. For flying, should I look only at a Friday-to-Monday three-night trip, or include a Thursday departure if it improves the schedule or fare?
Include Thursday evening, but show the extra hotel night separately. I mainly need to know whether the shorter three-night version still gives us enough time for the game and museum.

The strongest three-night flights are nonstop: depart ORD Friday at 6:20 p.m., arrive PIT at 8:50 p.m.; return Monday at 7:05 a.m., arriving ORD at 7:45 a.m. The three tickets total $927. Estimated ORD ground transportation or parking is $72, and Pittsburgh airport transportation plus local rides is about $110, putting transportation at roughly $1,109 before lodging.
What does that actually leave us in Pittsburgh? That Monday flight sounds very early.

You would likely leave home around 3:45 p.m. Friday and reach the hotel around 10:00 p.m. Eastern. Monday would require leaving the hotel about 5:00 a.m. You would have essentially no usable time Friday or Monday, but Saturday remains open for the 1:35 game and Sunday is fully available for the museum.
Check the museum hours against that. We do not need to pack anything else into Sunday.

Using the posted Sunday hours of 10:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., the museum fits comfortably. Even allowing 30 minutes each way from a central hotel, you could arrive at opening and stay through midafternoon or closing. The Saturday game also fits without pressure because the flight arrives the prior evening.
Now compare the Thursday flight and driving. Include tolls, fuel, and hotel parking for the car.

The Thursday-to-Monday nonstop schedule departs ORD at 6:20 p.m. Thursday and returns from PIT at 6:10 p.m. Monday. Airfare is $774 for three. With about $72 at ORD and $110 for Pittsburgh transportation, the flight-side total is about $956, but it requires four hotel nights. It gives you all day Friday and usable time until roughly 2:30 p.m. Monday.

Driving is about 470 miles each way. Allow 8 hours 15 minutes behind the wheel and roughly 9 hours door to door with stops and the time-zone change reflected on arrival. Estimated round-trip fuel is $132, tolls $56, and three nights of hotel parking about $90, for $278 total.
Put the driving schedule next to the two flight schedules. Assume we leave at 7:00 Friday morning and head home at 8:00 Monday morning.

Driving: leave Chicago at 7:00 a.m. Central Friday and reach the hotel around 5:00 p.m. Eastern. Leave Pittsburgh at 8:00 a.m. Eastern Monday and arrive home around 3:15 p.m. Central. Usable Pittsburgh time is Friday evening, all Saturday and Sunday, and no meaningful Monday activity time. Cost is about $278 plus three hotel nights.

Three-night flight: reach the hotel around 10:00 p.m. Friday and leave at 5:00 a.m. Monday. Usable time is Saturday and Sunday only. Transportation is about $1,109 plus three hotel nights.

Four-night flight: reach the hotel around 10:00 p.m. Thursday and leave around 2:30 p.m. Monday. Usable time is all Friday, Saturday, Sunday, and Monday morning. Transportation is about $956 plus four hotel nights.
So the short flight does not buy us any extra activity time over driving, correct? It only reduces the hours in transit.

Correct. Both structures fully protect the Saturday game and Sunday museum visit. The three-night flight cuts each travel day to roughly 4 hours 15 minutes door to door instead of about 9 hours driving, but its late Friday arrival and early Monday departure do not create another usable activity block. It costs about $831 more than driving before lodging.
Then use driving as the lead structure for the hotel search. Keep the three-night flight as the backup and the Thursday flight as the time-maximizing alternative. Nothing purchased.

Nothing has been purchased. I will carry three structures into the hotel comparison: lead option, drive Friday through Monday for about $278 and three hotel nights; backup, the three-night nonstop flights at $927 for three fares and about $1,109 including estimated ground transportation; and time-maximizing alternative, the Thursday-to-Monday flights at $774 for three fares and about $956 with ground transportation, plus a fourth hotel night. The hotel search will account for parking on the driving option and compare locations convenient to both the 1:35 p.m. Saturday game and the Carnegie Science Center’s 10:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m. Sunday hours.
